source.title: On Memorization in Probabilistic Deep Generative Models
source.citation: Gerrit J. J. van den Burg et al., 2021
source.authors: Gerrit J. J. van den Burg; C. Williams

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies memorization in probabilistic generative models and discusses its distinction from overfitting. Its experiments do not test the listed supervised-learning claim versions or their named measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports VAE memorization scores, their relation to train/test loss gaps, and comparisons with nearest-neighbor scores. These are findings about generative-model memorization, not the behaviors measured by the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The experiments measure local memorization in VAE density estimation, rather than any behavior specified by V1–V8. They do not compare random and natural labels, sweep width, compare classifier architectures or optimizers, vary batch size or dropout, measure sharpness, or test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples. Extending Feldman and Zhang's memorization measure does not test V8's removal result.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors introduce a likelihood-based memorization score and demonstrate local memorization in VAEs, including before a generalization gap develops and for observations that are not unlikely under the model. The tested nearest-neighbor ratio does not reliably capture this instance-level phenomenon, although nearest-neighbor methods may detect aggregate memorization.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains VAEs for unsupervised density estimation and measures changes in observation likelihood under cross-validation; the listed versions concern supervised classifiers and their generalization properties.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the observed loss-gap and memorization-score behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST VAEs have a visible loss gap at learning rate 10^-3 and no visible gap at 10^-4, yet substantial local memorization occurs without a gap and before one develops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A train-test loss gap is insufficient to detect local memorization in probabilistic generative models.

fits_no_version.finding: The CelebA VAE shows no strong general correlation between the proposed memorization score and the tested nearest-neighbor distance ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested nearest-neighbor distance ratio does not reliably track instance-level likelihood-based memorization in VAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: More than half of the CelebA observations in the highest 5% of memorization scores fall within the central 90% of model log probabilities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Highly memorized observations need not have unusually low likelihood when included in a generative model's training data.

record.problems: The authors state that hyperparameter settings were not extensively optimized. The work focuses on VAEs and uses a proposed memorization score; the authors say score distributions and probability differences are not necessarily comparable between datasets. The nearest-neighbor comparison depends on sampling and a chosen pixel-space distance metric.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels under matching training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier test error and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects on classifier test error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows describe the study's own results, but none bears on V1–V8. The supplementary MNIST results reinforce the generative-model findings without testing a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance in the specified classifiers and datasets.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their test-error effects.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on classifier held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Removing examples selected for memorization and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: VAE trained on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and test loss curves at two learning rates.
rows.measure: Train-test loss gap during training; the text says a clear generalization gap appears and the test loss has not yet started to increase.
rows.value: Clear generalization gap; test loss has not yet started to increase.
rows.note: This is a generative-model loss gap, not one of the listed version-specific classification measures.
rows.check: Accurately reports the VAE loss gap, but this learning-rate comparison measures no listed version.

rows.subject: VAE trained on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and test loss curves at two learning rates.
rows.measure: Train-test loss gap during training; the text says the gap seen at η = 10−3 disappears at this learning rate.
rows.note: The measure concerns VAE loss curves, not the classifier generalization behavior in the listed versions.
rows.check: Accurately reports disappearance of the VAE loss gap; this is not evidence of absence for any listed version.

rows.subject: VAE trained on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorization-score quantiles during training at two learning rates.
rows.measure: Memorization-score quantiles increase during training and take large values before the generalization gap appears.
rows.value: Large memorization-score quantiles before the generalization gap appears.
rows.note: The paper says these results show that the loss gap is insufficient to determine memorization.
rows.check: Accurately reports early growth of VAE memorization scores, which does not measure V1's random-label fitting or V8's test-accuracy removal effect.

rows.subject: VAE trained on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorization-score quantiles during training at two learning rates.
rows.measure: Memorization-score quantiles increase during training; the text says scores are reduced by lowering the learning rate, but relatively high values still occur.
rows.note: The about-80 maximum is explicitly stated in the text; this is a memorization measure, not a listed claim-version measure.
rows.check: The approximately 80 value is the maximum final memorization score, not either specified quantile. Separate that outcome from the quantile trajectories or correct the measure and conditions. Neither outcome measures a listed version.

rows.subject: VAE trained on CelebA
rows.operation_detail: Compared the proposed memorization score with a nearest-neighbor distance ratio.

conditions.value: Euclidean distance between images in pixel space after downsampling by a factor of 2

rows.measure: Relationship between memorization score and nearest-neighbor ratio; the text reports no strong correlation in general.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence interval of the standard error of the mean for distance-ratio measurements in each bin; no interval values stated in text.
rows.note: This compares two measures of generative-model memorization, not a generalization-gap property named in the versions.
rows.check: Accurately reports the comparison between two generative-model memorization measures; neither is V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: VAE trained on CelebA
rows.operation_detail: Binned observations by log probability and counted highly memorized observations, defined as the top 5% by memorization score.
rows.measure: More than half of highly memorized observations fall within the central 90% of log probability values, stated as log PA(x | D) ∈ [−14500, −12000].
rows.note: The reported outcome concerns likelihood and memorization in a generative model.
rows.check: Accurately reports likelihoods of highly memorized observations, without measuring test accuracy after their removal as required by V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
